capability: Deterministic foundation candidate-envelope runtime that is the platform's single input surface for every downstream module. CandidateEnvelope::from_bytes(bytes) or from_value(value) enforces: (a) parse_json_strict with MAX_JSON_BYTES=8_388_608 (8 MiB) request-size limit, MAX_JSON_DEPTH=64 nesting limit, MAX_COLLECTION_ENTRIES=100_000 array/object entry cap, valid UTF-8, no non-finite numbers (NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity), no duplicate JSON keys; (b) candidate object required (top-level array/scalar rejected); (c) candidate_id non-empty string; (d) candidate_type in {molecule, formulation, evidence_package}; (e) matching payload field per type (molecule/formulation/evidence_refs); (f) chemistry_v2 fields (inchi, inchi_key, mol, sdf, recipe_csv, etc.) require schema_version='amphora.candidate-envelope.v2' opt-in AND the pinned RDKit normalization boundary (currently unavailable → ChemistryNormalizationUnavailable); (g) computes original_bytes_sha256 = SHA-256(input bytes) and contract_hash_v1 = stable_hash(canonicalized value) for downstream binding. Every downstream module (all 24 already at Phase-0) receives this validated envelope; the runtime is the platform's front door.
population: Three positive candidates (molecule CCl4 solvent, formulation epoxy-polyamide primer 100+25 g, evidence_package lab measurement) plus 18 adversarial probes covering: top-level envelope non-object (array, string), candidate_id missing/empty/integer, candidate_type missing/unknown, payload_mismatch per type (molecule/formulation/evidence_package), chemistry_v2 opt-in cases (v2 field without opt-in; v2 opt-in without RDKit boundary), and 7 strict-JSON parse probes (malformed trailing comma, size >8 MiB, non-UTF-8 bytes, duplicate top-level keys, IEEE-754 NaN, IEEE-754 Infinity, 100-level nesting depth-exhaustion).
split_methodology: No fitting - candidate-contract validation is closed-form JSON parsing + strict field-presence + type-match + hash-computation. The harness constructs 3 positive scenarios + 18 adversarial probes in-Rust and asserts (a) positive from_bytes returns Ok with candidate_id/candidate_type matching input, (b) original_bytes_sha256 equals independently-computed SHA-256 of input bytes bit-exact, (c) contract_hash_v1 stable across two from_bytes constructions, (d) from_bytes and from_value produce equal contract_hash_v1 (canonical-JSON invariant), (e) each adversarial probe returns Err matching a specific ContractError variant. Byte-stability across replays confirmed.
theory: IETF RFC 8259 (2017) 'The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format' - the JSON grammar and interoperability requirements that strict parsing enforces. IETF RFC 8785 (2020) 'JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)' - canonical serialization foundation for reproducible contract_hash_v1 that agrees across from_bytes and from_value. OWASP Top 10 A08:2021 'Software and Data Integrity Failures' - integrity verification methodology for input surfaces. OWASP JSON Parser Safety Guidance (2020) - defensive parser design against deeply-nested and oversized input. IEEE 754-2019 'IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic' Section 6 (Infinity, NaN semantics) - the non-finite number semantics that strict JSON rejects since RFC 8259 disallows Infinity/NaN literals. CWE-121 'Stack-based Buffer Overflow' + CWE-400 'Uncontrolled Resource Consumption' - depth-exhaustion and size-exhaustion attack classes that MAX_JSON_DEPTH=64 and MAX_JSON_BYTES=8_388_608 mitigate. CWE-20 'Improper Input Validation' - the general class this runtime addresses. NIST FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 (2015) - hash function for original_bytes_sha256 and stable_hash. Salzer 1975 'The Protection of Information in Computer Systems' Proceedings of the IEEE 63(9):1278-1308 - least-privilege and complete-mediation methodology. Anderson 1980 'Computer Security Threat Monitoring and Surveillance' - reference-monitor pattern applied at the input surface: every candidate is validated once at the boundary and downstream modules trust only the resulting envelope.

fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.prediction_rule: For each input bytes / value: (1) if bytes: check size <= 8_388_608 (else RequestTooLarge), UTF-8 (else InvalidUtf8), strict-parse via StrictSeed with depth budget 64 and entry budget 100_000 rejecting non-finite numbers and duplicate keys (else InvalidJson); (2) verify top-level is a JSON object (else CandidateNotObject); (3) verify candidate_id is non-empty string (else InvalidCandidateId); (4) verify candidate_type in {molecule, formulation, evidence_package} (else InvalidCandidateType); (5) verify matching payload field is a JSON object (else PayloadMismatch); (6) if any chemistry_v2 key present, require schema_version='amphora.candidate-envelope.v2' opt-in (else PayloadMismatch) and reject if RDKit normalization boundary unavailable (ChemistryNormalizationUnavailable); (7) compute original_bytes_sha256 = SHA-256(input bytes) OR SHA-256(canonicalized(value)) for from_value path; (8) compute contract_hash_v1 = stable_hash(canonical value); (9) return CandidateEnvelope { value, original_bytes_sha256, contract_hash_v1 }. Runtime never accepts NaN, Infinity, duplicate keys, oversized input, or overly-deep nesting.
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.note: Foundational strict-JSON envelope validator. No parameters to learn; the theory is RFC 8259 JSON grammar + RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization + OWASP A08:2021 + OWASP JSON parser safety + IEEE 754 non-finite semantics + CWE-121/400 depth/size exhaustion mitigation + NIST FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 + Salzer 1975 complete-mediation + Anderson 1980 reference-monitor.

dataset_fixture_note: candidate-contract Phase-0 harness constructs its 3 positive scenarios + 18 adversarial probes in-Rust and does not consume an external fixture. SHA-256 recorded is the on-disk benchmark-lock hash.
